summary: San Leandro sits on a flat, industrial-edged stretch of the East Bay shoreline where motor vehicle theft runs at roughly 2,247 per 100,000 — one of the highest rates you'll encounter in the Bay Area's mid-tier cities, and a number worth understanding before signing a lease. The city is squeezed between Oakland to the north and Hayward to the south along the I-880 corridor, and that freeway acts as a physical spine that cleaves neighborhoods from the waterfront; the bay itself is right there, with a shoreline trail offering wide-open views toward the San Francisco skyline, yet much of the western edge is buffered by marshland and industrial parcels rather than boardwalks. At a median home price of $813,600 against a median household income of $98,063, the price-to-income ratio lands around 8.3× — steep, but meaningfully below neighboring Oakland or Fremont, which is partly why the city functions as a bedroom community for workers commuting to larger job centers via BART, which has a station centrally located in the city's downtown. That downtown has been slowly adding sit-down restaurants and a craft brewery cluster, though the retail texture still leans heavily toward strip-mall corridors along East 14th Street. The climate is remarkably mild — annual highs average 67°F with nine hours of daily sunshine and lows rarely dipping below 50°F — making the Marina Park shoreline walkable year-round. San Leandro offers Bay Area geography at a slight discount, but the tradeoff is a city still negotiating the tension between its legacy as a manufacturing hub and its gradual reinvention as something more walkable and self-contained.
